title: Mount
subject: gated-scoped-ac
summary: How an app builds the engine and the gate once, from its config and its tables, and puts the hydration middleware in front of its routes.

axioms.text: The engine and the gate are built once, at boot, in the app shell. Nothing builds them per request.
The app owns the map from the config's entity names to its drizzle tables. It is the one place both vocabularies meet.
Slices receive the engine and the gate factory at mount; they never build or configure them.
Hydration runs after the session middleware and before every route that reads the [[access context]].

purpose.intro: Three steps make the library live in an app: build the engine, build the gate over the database handle, and mount the middleware that builds each request's context. In this repo the first two are `apps/main/core/api/src/access-control.ts`.
purpose.note: Writing the config itself is [[gated-scoped-ac-dsl-rules|DSL rules]]; what the context holds is [[gated-scoped-ac-bag|Access context]].

reference.statement: `createAc(config)` takes the loaded config and the tables, and returns the engine.

imagesAndDiagrams.value:
| Field | What it is |
|---|---|
| `tables` | entity name → drizzle table (or view); every entity a permission names |
| `permissions` | the map `registerPermissions` returned |
| `accountBaseline` | the forest of user roles |
| `forests` | org type → its forest |
| `visibilityJoins` | optional: per entity, other entities whose readable rows also make a row readable, as `{ via, fk }` |
| `orgTypePath` | optional: where the org type sits in the bag; default `$session.organization.type` |

reference.statement: `createGatedDb(rawDb, deps)` takes the database handle and returns the gate factory: `gatedDb(bag)` gives a request's [[gated db]], `gatedDb.ungated()` the raw handle.

claims.text: `deps.tables`: the same map the engine has. `deps.engine`: the engine, used for the create verdict.

`deps.idColumns`: per entity, the primary-key column when it is not `id`. The gate keys every write and every visibility channel by it, so a table keyed by `userId` must name it or its writes match nothing.
One factory per handle. A second handle over the same database, such as one that versions a table, gets its own `createGatedDb` with the same deps.

`ungated()` is the one named path past access control: hydration's own reads, and the reads and writes no rule covers (writes before a session exists, lookups, side-effect writes). Nothing reachable from a route by itself may use it.

reference.statement: The main API builds both in `access-control.ts`, hands them to the slices in `mounts.ts`, and mounts hydration in `routes/client.ts`.

examples.title: Handing them to the slices, and mounting hydration

export const userOrg = mountUserOrgApi({ engine: acEngine, gatedDb, baselineRoles, /* … */ });
export const credits = mountCreditsApi({ engine: acEngine, /* … */ });

snippets.caption: `apps/main/core/api/src/routes/client.ts`: session, then hydration, then the routes

reference.topic: Another app over the same database
reference.statement: An app that serves the same data builds its own engine and gate from the same config and the tables it serves, and the same context per request. open-api does: `apps/open-api/src/access-control.ts` builds them, and its acting-session middleware builds the context of the user a delegated request acts for.
A slice declares the narrowest engine and gate it needs, and the app satisfies them at mount.

claims.text: A slice declares the engine as `Pick<Ac, …>` of exactly the calls it makes, and the gate as `(bag: unknown) => GatedDb<SchemaTables>`, so a test can hand it a stub.
A slice that needs the ungated handle for its named exceptions declares `ungated()` on that factory type, and says in its repository why each use is one.
